note: Opened by T-1250 to rule on the sentence 'the Illinois Central's 1852 trestle then fixed the line' (docs/research/01-terrain-hydrology.md sec 4), which the e1871_postfire epoch used to repeat. It reads: 'In 1852 the Illinois Central built a trestle about 300 feet east of Michigan Avenue and the breakwater a little farther out. This left a substantial lagoon extending south to 12th street where the railroad came on shore.' So the 1852 trestle is sourced here, and so is the refusal of the sentence as written: north of Twelfth Street the trestle stood OUT in the lake with water behind it, which is the opposite of fixing the shore, and south of Twelfth -- the whole of the Prairie Avenue reach -- the railroad ran on the shore and no trestle is described at all.
what_it_supplies: That the Illinois Central built a trestle about 300 ft east of Michigan Avenue in 1852, with a breakwater beyond it and a lagoon behind it as far south as 12th Street
